_comment: Eastern Cape Department of Education Grade 10 Geography P2 (Mapwork), November 2019 provincial common examination.
Questions and marking-guideline answers extracted from the text layer of the official PDFs
(paper2.pdf, paper2_memo.pdf) and read against the rendered pages. Figures, maps,
graphs and photographs are described in [FIGURE: ...] brackets inside 'context'. memo_answer is
from the official marking guideline (English); mark allocations such as (2) are kept, one
accepted point per line. Column A/B items use the Grade 12 '[Y ... / Z ...]' style.
FORMAT: one 1½-hour paper answered in the question paper, 75 marks, all questions compulsory:
Question 1 multiple choice (15), Section B Question 2 mapwork calculations and techniques (20),
Question 3 map and photo application and interpretation (25), Question 4 GIS (15). It is based on
the 1 : 50 000 topographic map 2730DD VRYHEID and the 1 : 10 000 orthophoto map 2730DD 2 VRYHEID
EAST, which schools collected separately; the map sheets were not published with the paper, so
map-read inputs come from the memo's accepted values. Multiple-choice answers are the boxed letters
OFFICIAL MEMO ERRORS (see memo_note): 2.1.1 gives 34 km for 3,4 cm on the 1 : 10 000 orthophoto map;

questions.context: GENERAL INFORMATION ON VRYHEID: The town of Vryheid in KwaZulu-Natal Province lies southward along the R33 in the valley at the foot of the Zungwini Mountain. It is the centre of coal mining and cattle farming in the district and being an old town with a historical past, there are a number of national monuments in the town. Decisive battles were fought in the vicinity during the Anglo Boer War. [FIGURE: outline map of South Africa's provinces with Vryheid marked in northern KwaZulu-Natal.] Coordinates: 27° 46' 3" S, 30° 47' 9" E. Glossary on the map: Landing strip - Vliegveld; Furrow - Voor; Caravan Park - Karavaanpark; Canal - Kanaal; Sewerage works - Rioolwerke; Golf Course - Gholfbaan; Excavation - Uitgrawing; Nature reserve - Natuurreservaat; Rifle Range - Skietbaan; Aerodrome - Vliegveld; Ravine - Kloof. | QUESTION 1: MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTIONS. questions.context: SECTION B: MAPWORK CALCULATIONS AND TECHNIQUES. QUESTION 2 | 2.1 Refer to the orthophoto map.
questions.text: Measure and calculate the distance between points 1 and 2 in kilometres.
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: Map skills and calculations
questions.memo_answer:
Distance = cm / scale x 100 000
3,4 cm / 10 000 x 100 000 [Range: 3,3-3,5 cm]
= 34 km [Range: 33-35 km]
questions.memo_note: Official memo error: 3,4 cm on the 1 : 10 000 orthophoto map is 3,4 x 10 000 = 34 000 cm = 0,34 km (range 0,33-0,35 km), not 34 km.

questions.text: Calculate the area on the orthophoto map (also indicated by a black rectangular box on the topographic map). Use the formula: AREA = LENGTH X BREADTH
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: Map skills and calculations
questions.memo_answer:
AREA = LENGTH x WIDTH (measured on the black box on the 1 : 50 000 topographic map)
Length = 8,2 cm x 0,5 [8,1 cm-8,3 cm] = 4,1 km
Width = 5,8 cm x 0,5 [5,7 cm-5,9 cm] = 2,9 km
Area = 4,1 x 2,9 = 11,89 km² [Range = 11,5-12,24 km²]

questions.text: Describe the difference between an oblique and a vertical photograph.
questions.topic: Geographical Skills and Techniques: GIS
questions.memo_answer:
In vertical photographs the camera is perpendicular / vertical above the earth’s surface / taken from the air
In oblique photographs the camera is tilted/slanting at an angle
Objects behind high features like hills or buildings are obscured/ hidden in oblique
Objects below appear from their roof top
Scale varies within the same photographs in oblique / Objects in the foreground appear larger than those in the background
The scale is nearly the same for vertical photographs [Any ONE]
